mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% triggers strong labor demand, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE does not fall below 3.5% or 5-day returns are not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (demand) and industrial production (supply) above thresholds signals robust economic expansion, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Proxies do not rise together or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a 'late-cycle expansion' with FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and CPIAUCSL < 260, accommodative monetary policy and controlled inflation boost equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: late-cycle expansion with FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and CPIAUCSL < 260
failure_condition: Regime conditions not met or 20-day returns not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained quarterly GDP growth above 5% signals robust demand, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: GDP growth does not sustain 5% quarterly or returns not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production exceeding 110 triggers a supply-driven upturn, reducing production costs and boosting corporate margins, resulting in positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not cross 110 or returns not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) and GDP growth (GDPC1) above thresholds indicate labor market tightness and economic expansion, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Proxies do not rise together or returns not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a 'post-shock recovery' regime with UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 3%, labor market strengthening and accommodative policy lower risk premiums, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: post-shock recovery with UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: Regime conditions not met or returns not positive (p > 0.05).
